{{Short description|Australian snack food manufacturer}} {{Use dmy dates|date=October 2018}} {{Use Australian English|date=July 2013}} {{Infobox company | name = Arnott's Group | logo = Arnotts logo.jpg | image = Arnott's Distribution Centre in Huntingwood (1).jpg | image_caption = Arnott's Distribution Centre in [[Huntingwood]], [[Sydney]] | former_name = {{Unbulleted list|William Arnotts, Morrow|Australian Biscuit Company|Arnott's Biscuits Limited|Campbell Arnott's}} | type = [[Subsidiary]] | industry = [[Biscuits]]
[[Snack food]] | founded = {{Start date and age|1865}} | hq_location = [[North Strathfield]], Sydney, New South Wales, Australia | area_served = Worldwide | products = {{hlist|[[SAO (biscuit)|SAO]]|[[Jatz]]|[[Arnott's Shapes|Shapes]]|[[Tim Tam]]s|[[Iced Vovo]]s|[[Tiny Teddy|Tiny Teddies]]|[[Marie biscuit|Marie]]|[[Nice (biscuit)|Nice]]|[[Monte Carlo (biscuit)|Monte Carlo]]|[[Ginger snap|Ginger Nut]]|[[Wagon Wheels]]|[[Campbell's]] (outside North America and Mexico)}} | revenue = [[Australian dollar|A$]]1.04 billion | revenue_year = 2018 | num_employees = | num_employees_year = | parent = [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts|KKR]] | website = {{URL|https://arnotts.com/}} }} '''Arnott's Group''' is an Australian producer of [[biscuits]] and [[snack food]]. Founded in 1865 by [[William Arnott (biscuit manufacturer)|William Arnott]], the first factory was Arnott's Steam Biscuit Factory in [[Newcastle, New South Wales]]. The company undertook several mergers and acquisitions in the 1950s and 1960s, Arnott's was acquired by the [[Campbell Soup Company]] in 1997, before being sold to American global private investment company [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts]] (KKR) in 2019, of which it is now a subsidiary. They are the largest producer of biscuits in Australia, and are particularly known for sweet varieties such as [[Tim Tams]], [[Iced VoVo]]s, and [[Tiny Teddy|Tiny Teddies]], and savoury crackers such as [[Jatz]], [[Arnott's Shapes|Shapes]] and [[SAO (biscuit)|SAO]]s. ==History== [[File:William Arnott, circa 1869.jpg|thumb|upright|Arnott's founder [[William Arnott (biscuit manufacturer)|William Arnott]]]] Scottish immigrant [[William Arnott (biscuit manufacturer)|William Arnott]] opened a bakery in [[Morpeth, New South Wales]] in 1847{{cite web |title=Aussie legend Arnott's up for sale |website=retailworldmagazine.com.au |date=1 September 2018 |url=https://retailworldmagazine.com.au/aussie-legend-arnotts-up-for-sale/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220526103043/https://retailworldmagazine.com.au/aussie-legend-arnotts-up-for-sale/ |archive-date=26 May 2022 |url-status=dead |access-date=30 January 2026}} or 1848.{{cite web |last=O'Connell |first=Jan |title=Arnott's Steam Biscuit factory |website=Australian Food Timeline |date=14 December 2022 |url=https://australianfoodtimeline.com.au/arnotts-factory-opens/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250225035633/https://australianfoodtimeline.com.au/arnotts-factory-opens/ |archive-date=25 February 2025 |url-status=live |access-date=30 January 2026}} In 1865 he moved to a bakery on [[Hunter Street, Newcastle]], providing bread, pies and biscuits for the townspeople and the ships docking at the local port.{{Cite web|url=http://www.arnotts.com/about-us/arnotts-heritage.aspx|title=Our heritage|website=Arnott's Australia: Arnott's heritage|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326190604/http://www.arnotts.com/about-us/arnotts-heritage.aspx|archive-date=26 March 2015|url-status=dead|access-date=25 October 2018}} In 1875, Arnott's Steam Biscuit Factory was established in Newcastle and started producing various types of plain and sweet biscuits and cakes. In the 1880s biscuits were sent from the factory to [[Sydney]] first by ship, and then later by road. A new factory began operations in Sydney in 1875. In 1949 it merged with Morrows Pty Ltd, a [[Brisbane]] biscuit manufacturer, forming William Arnotts, Morrow Pty Ltd.{{cite news|date=31 December 1949|title=Advertising|page=3|newspaper=[[The Courier-Mail]]|issue=4087|location=Queensland, Australia|url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article49700955|url-status=live|access-date=15 September 2020|via=National Library of Australia|archive-date=15 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200915093534/https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/49700955}} In 1950 William Arnott Pty. Ltd. purchased a half share in [[Adelaide]] biscuit manufacturers [[Motteram & Sons]], which in 1952 became known as Arnott Motteram Ltd (or Arnott's-Motteram).{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article47422487 |title=Biscuit Makers Change Name |newspaper=[[The Advertiser (Adelaide)|The Advertiser]] |location=Adelaide |date=3 July 1952 |access-date=19 August 2014 |page=5 |via=National Library of Australia}}{{Cite web |title=Adelaide's Motteram biscuit legacy lost in the mesh with Menz and Arnott's takeover |url=https://adelaideaz.com/articles/adelaide-s-motteram-biscuit-legacy-lost-in-mesh-with-menz-and-arnott-s-takeover |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=adelaideaz.com}}{{cite web |title=Motteram & Sons: A family biscuit company |website=State Library of South Australia |date=6 February 1926 |url=https://www.slsa.sa.gov.au/motteram-sons-a-family-biscuit-company |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260129225942/https://www.slsa.sa.gov.au/motteram-sons-a-family-biscuit-company |archive-date=29 January 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=29 January 2026}} Further acquisitions and mergers took place, for a while including [[Menz Confectionery]], with the company renamed Arnott-Motteram-Menz. The Australian Biscuit Company was later renamed Arnott's Biscuits Pty Ltd.{{Cite web |date=1990-02-16 |title=ARNOTTS GOES BACK TO BISCUIT BASICS |url=https://www.afr.com/companies/arnotts-goes-back-to-biscuit-basics-19900216-kalqc |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=[[Australian Financial Review]]|language=en}} Other companies absorbed in the mergers included [[Brockhoff Biscuits]],{{Cite news |date=1963-06-06 |title=Biscuit Firms Plan Merger |work=[[Canberra Times]] |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article131722165 |access-date=2022-04-04}} Guest's Biscuits{{Cite web |date=2021-09-24 |title=A Cracker Of An Idea That Really Took The Biscuit-2021 News |url=https://hillstohawkesbury.com.au/a-cracker-of-an-idea-that-really-biscuit/ |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=hillstohawkesbury.com.au |language=en-GB}} in Victoria, and [[Mills and Ware]] in [[Western Australia]].{{Cite web |date=2021-09-24 |title=Remembering Mills and Ware |url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/community-news/south/marys-memories-looking-back-at-biscuit-and-cake-empire-mills-and-ware--c-3909940 |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=Community News |language=en}} [[File:Arnotts.jpg|thumb|Biscuit tin on display in museum at [[Young, New South Wales]]]] Until 1975 the company was under family control, with the descendants of William Arnott, including [[Halse Rogers Arnott]] and [[Geoffrey H. Arnott]], acting as Chairman.{{Citation needed|date=March 2025}} In 1997, Arnott's Biscuits was subject to an [[extortion]] bid by Queenslander Joy Ellen Thomas, aged 72 years,{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2002/04/26/1019441296856.html|title=Biscuit extortion case dropped over DNA hurdle|date=27 April 2002|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924115921/http://www.smh.com.au/articles/2002/04/26/1019441296856.html|archive-date=24 September 2015}} who allegedly threatened to poison packets of Arnott's Monte Carlo biscuits in [[South Australia]] and [[Victoria (state)|Victoria]]. The company conducted a massive recall and publicity campaign, publishing the extortionist's threats and demands in full-page newspaper ads.[[Radio National]] (PM): [http://www.abc.net.au/pm/stories/s111445.htm Herron's actions a contrast to Arnotts' open-ness] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041201150049/http://www.abc.net.au/pm/stories/s111445.htm |date=1 December 2004 }}, [[ABC Radio National|ABC Radio]], 17 March 2000. Thomas was not charged with any offence as the prosecution dropped the case against her because of conflicting evidence. The recall cost the company [[A$]]22 million, but Arnott's was praised for its openness and honesty in dealing with the crisis.''[[The 7.30 Report]]'': [http://www.abc.net.au/7.30/content/2005/s1406752.htm Mars, snickers threat aimed at unnamed organisation] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060409080910/http://www.abc.net.au/7.30/content/2005/s1406752.htm |date=9 April 2006 }}, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]], 4 July 2005. [[File:Arnott's Biscuits Advert 1932.jpg|thumb|upright|1932 advertisement for Arnott's Biscuits]] In 1997, the [[Campbell Soup Company]] of North America, a shareholder of Arnott's since the 1980s, acquired Arnott's in full. Thus, in 1997, Arnott's Biscuits Ltd became a wholly owned subsidiary of the Campbell Soup Company.{{Cite web |date=1990-09-28 |title=Arnott's ownership passed to Campbell's - Australian food history timeline |url=https://australianfoodtimeline.com.au/arnotts-ownership/ |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=Australian Food Timeline |language=en-AU}} This caused a significant amount of controversy in Australia, based on the desire for such an Australian icon to remain in Australian hands, and a fear that Campbell's would [[Americanization|Americanise]] the products.{{Cite web |last=Druce |first=Alex |date=2019-07-24 |title=Arnott's gobbled up in $US2.2bn sale |url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6294703/arnotts-gobbled-up-in-us22bn-sale/ |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=The Canberra Times |language=en-AU}} Manufacturing of Arnott's biscuits, however, remained in Australia, and as part of a long-term expansion plan, Arnott's closed its [[Melbourne]] factory in September 2002.Moynihan, Stephen: [http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2002/08/02/1028157844462.html Tearful workers feel the final crunch at Arnott's] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030418022541/http://www.theage.com.au/articles/2002/08/02/1028157844462.html |date=18 April 2003 }}, ''[[The Age]]'', 3 August 2002. In the mid-2000s the company stated that it held over 70 per cent of the Australian market, with 97 per cent of Australian homes using its products. In 2002, Arnott's acquired [[Snack Foods Limited]].Business Breakfast: [http://www.abc.net.au/businessbreakfast/content/2002/s574846.htm Arnotts bids for Snack Foods] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071205135925/http://www.abc.net.au/businessbreakfast/content/2002/s574846.htm |date=5 December 2007 }}, [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation]], 6 July 2002. In April 2008, Campbell Arnott's sold Arnott's Snackfoods to The Real McCoy Snackfood Co. and the company became known as [[Snack Brands Australia]].{{Cite web |date=2008-04-28 |title=The Real McCoy Snackfood Co buys Arnotts snack foods {{!}} Shop Ethical! |url=https://www.ethical.org.au/3.4.2/blog/the-real-mccoy-snackfood-co-buys-arnotts-snack-foods/ |access-date=2022-04-04 |website=www.ethical.org.au |language=en-AU}} Campbell's put Arnott's up for auction in mid- 2018. In July 2019, Campbell Soup Company agreed to sell Arnott's to [[Kohlberg Kravis Roberts]] (KKR), an American private equity group, for $US2.2 billion.{{cite news |title=Arnott's sold by Campbells to KKR |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-07-24/arnotts-sold-by-campbells-to-private-equity-group-kkr/11341190 |access-date=24 July 2019 |work=ABC News |agency=ABC News |date=24 July 2019 |ref=15 |archive-date=25 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190725163057/https://www.abc.net.au/news/2019-07-24/arnotts-sold-by-campbells-to-private-equity-group-kkr/11341190 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/business/companies/barbarians-snatch-tim-tams-arnott-s-set-to-be-acquired-by-kkr-in-3b-deal-20190724-p52a71.html|title=Barbarians snatch Tim Tams? Arnott's set to be acquired by KKR in $3b deal|last=Powell|first=Dominic|date=2019-07-24|website=[[Sydney Morning Herald]]|language=en|access-date=2019-11-17|archive-date=17 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117232740/https://www.smh.com.au/business/companies/barbarians-snatch-tim-tams-arnott-s-set-to-be-acquired-by-kkr-in-3b-deal-20190724-p52a71.html|url-status=live}} Just weeks after the sale, Arnott's was in a public dispute with [[Woolworths (Australia)|Woolworths]], which reportedly wanted to charge higher prices for marketing displays.{{cite web |url=https://www.afr.com/companies/retail/arnott-s-in-stand-off-with-woolies-20190926-p52v61 |title=Arnott's in stand-off with Woolies |last=Mitchell |first=Sue |date=27 September 2019 |website=Australian Financial Review|publisher=Nine Entertainment |access-date=29 September 2019 |archive-date=26 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190926232429/https://www.afr.com/companies/retail/arnott-s-in-stand-off-with-woolies-20190926-p52v61 |url-status=live }} In August 2020, the company was renamed Arnott's Group.{{Cite web |last=Cameron |first=Nadia |date=2020-08-28 |title=Arnott's Group unveils new corporate logo and expansion plans |url=https://www.cmo.com.au/article/682504/arnott-group-unveils-new-corporate-logo-expansion-plans/ |access-date=2023-09-09 |website=CMO |language=en-au}} In December 2020, Arnott's announced it would acquire the cereal and snack company Freedom Foods Group for {{AUD|20 million}}.{{Cite web |last=Berry |first=Kim |date=17 December 2020 |title=Arnott's to buy Freedom Foods' cereals and snacks business for $20m |url=https://www.foodanddrinkbusiness.com.au/news/arnott-s-to-buy-freedom-foods-cereals-and-snacks-business-for-20m |access-date=9 September 2023 |website=Food & Drink Business |language=en}} In February 2021, Arnott's acquired a 75 per cent stake in Diver Foods. Arnott's established the Good Food Partners division to manage operations from the two acquisitions.{{Cite web |last=Berry |first=Kim |date=9 February 2021 |title=Arnott's continues acquisitions to grow cereal & snacks business |url=https://www.foodanddrinkbusiness.com.au/news/arnott-s-continues-acquisitions-to-grow-cereal-and-snacks-business |access-date=9 September 2023 |website=Food & Drink Business |language=en}} In May 2021, Arnott's acquired the New Zealand cracker company 180degrees.{{Cite web |last=Berry |first=Kim |date=14 May 2021 |title=Arnott's buys premium NZ cracker business |url=https://www.foodanddrinkbusiness.com.au/news/arnott-s-buys-premium-nz-cracker-business |access-date=9 September 2023 |website=Food & Drink Business |language=en}} In June 2023, Arnott's opened a new factory in [[Avondale, Auckland|Avondale]], New Zealand. It marked the company's return to manufacturing in the country after a 25-year absence.{{Cite web |last=Prasad |first=Alka |date=2023-09-10 |title=Watch: Arnott's new Auckland factory will cater for local tastes |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/business/watch-arnotts-new-auckland-factory-in-avondale-will-cater-for-local-tastes/43JL4KJEKFASDG6WFONFYUJC5E/ |access-date=2023-09-09 |website=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |language=en-NZ}} In August 2023, Arnott's opened a {{convert|43,000|m2|adj=on}} automated distribution centre at its [[Huntingwood]] site in Sydney.{{Cite web |last=Berry |first=Kim |date=2023-08-30 |title=Arnott's officially opens automated DC to drive growth plans |url=https://www.foodanddrinkbusiness.com.au/news/arnott-s-officially-opens-automated-dc-to-drive-growth-plans |access-date=2023-09-12 |website=Food & Drink Business |language=en}} ==Today== {{as of|January 2026}}, the Arnott's Group is headquartered in Sydney. Its brands include Campbell's, V8, Messy Monkeys, Freedom Cereals and 180Degrees. The company has more than 4,000 employees across the Asia Pacific region, including in its manufacturing operations in Australia, New Zealand, Malaysia, and Indonesia.{{cite web |title=The Arnott's Group: About Us |website=Arnott's |date=3 April 2023 |url=https://www.arnotts.com/articles/MISC/the-arnotts-group-about-us |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260103021744/https://www.arnotts.com/articles/MISC/the-arnotts-group-about-us |archive-date=3 January 2026 |url-status=live |access-date=30 January 2026}} Arnott's produces a wide range of foods, and is particularly known for its biscuits and snack foods.{{cite web|url=http://www.daff.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/2210992/Campbell-Arnotts.pdf|date=30 September 2012|title=Campbell Arnott's Submission to National Food Plan Green Paper|author=Campbell Arnott's|publisher=Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140908070306/http://www.daff.gov.au/__data/assets/pdf_file/0007/2210992/Campbell-Arnotts.pdf|archive-date=8 September 2014}} They are the largest producer of biscuits in Australia.{{cite web |last=Drake |first=Isobel |date=24 April 2009 |title=Arnott's issues ultimatum to Krispy Kreme |url=http://www.ausfoodnews.com.au/2009/04/24/arnotts-issues-ultimatum-to-krispy-kreme.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140908065654/http://ausfoodnews.com.au/2009/04/24/arnotts-issues-ultimatum-to-krispy-kreme.html |archive-date=8 September 2014 |publisher=Australian Food News}} ==Logo== The original Arnott's logo depicted a multi-coloured parrot sitting atop a T-shaped perch, eating a cracker biscuit. It is based on a Mexican parrot, or [[macaw]], given to William Arnott by the captain of a fleet of coal ships when he returned to Newcastle from Scotland in the 1870s. The logo was drawn by Arnott’s daughter-in-law, and registered as a logo in 1888.{{cite web | title=The Arnott's Biscuits logo – City of Canada Bay Heritage Society | website=City of Canada Bay Heritage Society – Hosting Sydney’s 2 best kept secrets | date=17 October 2023 | url=https://canadabayheritage.asn.au/the-arnotts-biscuits-logo/ | access-date=7 February 2026}} During a radio interview on ABC, William Arnott's great-great-great-grandson stated that the logo represents the proverb "Honesty is the best policy" where the phrase was constructed from "On his T, is the best pol' (polly) I see".{{Cite web | last=Arnott | first=Stephen | title=Baking an icon, the Arnott's way | website=ABC Radio | date=2023-10-04 | access-date=2024-11-25 | url=https://www.abc.net.au/listen/programs/newcastlecast/arnotts-biscuits-history-morpeth/102929916#:~:text=Stephen%20Arnott%3A%20So%20the%20parrot%27s%20really%20interesting%20in%20the%20sense%20that%20it%27s%20the%20colours%20of%20a%20rosella%2C%20but%20William%20wanted%20to%20do%20this%20as%20a%20slogan.%20So%20he%20looked%20at%20this%20and%20he%20said%2C%20well%2C%20uh%2C%20on%20its%20T%20is%20the%20best%20poll%20I%20see.%20Which%20means%20you%20came%20up%20with%20a%20slogan%20of%20honesty%20is%20the%20best%20policy.}} In 2020 Arnott’s announced a new corporate logo, incorporating a modern, streamlined version of the parrot. Australian consumers were shocked at the change, but the original logo was retained on the Australian biscuits. ==Products== [[File:Tim Tams.jpg|thumb|A plate of [[Tim Tam]]s]] Arnott's are well known in Australia and internationally for producing several quintessentially Australian biscuits. extract: Arnott's Group is an Australian producer of biscuits and snack food. Founded in 1865 by William Arnott, the first factory was Arnott's Steam Biscuit Factory in Newcastle, New South Wales. The company undertook several mergers and acquisitions in the 1950s and 1960s, Arnott's was acquired by the Campbell Soup Company in 1997, before being sold to  American global private investment company Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) in 2019, of which it is now a subsidiary. They are the largest producer of biscuits in Australia, and are particularly known for sweet varieties such as Tim Tams, Iced VoVos, and Tiny Teddies, and savoury crackers such as Jatz, Shapes and SAOs.
